chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Dawood narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Abu Malik al-Janbi narrated from Umar ibn Bashr al-Hamdani, saying: I asked Abu Ishaq: 'When were the people debased?'
He replied: 'When Al-Hussein (peace be upon him) was martyred, and Zyad was ascribed [to Abu Sufyan], and Hujr ibn Adi was killed.'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.حُجْرُ بْنُ عَدِيٍّ: Hujr ibn Adi, a companion of the Prophet and early Shia figure
key_terms.ذَلَّ: To be debased, humiliated, or lowered in status
key_terms.زِيَادٌ: Ziyad ibn Abihi, a prominent Umayyad governor

ai.seo_question: What three events caused the debasement of the people according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three pivotal moments to illustrate the shift from spiritual integrity to political consolidation in early Islam, where the martyrdom of Imam al-Hussein (AS) marked the peak of external oppression, while the other two events reflected internal structural changes. The inclusion of Ziyad’s fabricated lineage and Hujn ibn Adi’s execution underscores the Umayyad strategy of legitimizing rule through both genealogical claims and the suppression of prominent companions. This triad serves as a foundational narrative in Shia historiography for understanding the socio-political debasement of the community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-248 Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his grandfather quoted Davood, on the authority of Isa ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Salih, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Janby , on the authority of Umar ibn Bashr al-Hamedany, “I asked Abi Ishaq, ‘When were the people debased?’
He replied, ‘Since Al-Hussein (MGB) was martyred; Zyad was ascribed to Abu Sufyan ; and the killing of Hujr ibn Uday .’”
